To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new method for the survey and description of geomorphic units that is flexible and applicable to most fluvial conditions and that supports the characterisation of physical habitats at the reach scale.
we present a new system for surveying and classifying geomorphic units that is based on a hierarchical, multiscale approach and is applicable to most fluvial conditions.

a new system for survey and classification of the physical habitats of rivers, the geomorphic units survey (GUS) system, is presented and tested on a range of European rivers, including rivers in the UK, France, Germany, Spain and the Netherlands.

the development of a system for the characterisation of geomorphic units that is useful for the assessment of river hydomorphological conditions.
the development of a new system for characterising river geomorphic units and fluvial morphology that supports hydromorphologically based assessment and monitoring of rivers.
the development of a new methodological approach for the survey and assessment of geomorphological units and physical habitats.

the method presented here represents a significant improvement over existing methods and can be used for the survey of river geomorphic conditions and for the assessment of physical habitats at the reach scale.

the proposed system is a flexible and applicable method for the characterisation of river physical habitats and fl uvial hydromor phology, and can be used for the assessment of hydromorphol ogical conditions at the reach level, in support of the implementation of the WFD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geomorphic units survey is a method for surveying the physical habitat and the hydromorphologic features of rivers at the reach scale.

we have developed a new system for characterising and classifying geomorphic units, which is embedded into a geomorphological framework and which supports the assessment of river hydomorphological conditions at reach scale.
the geomorphic units survey method can be applied to any river, regardless of size and type, for a variety of purposes and scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the survey and assessment of geomorphology and physical habitats at the reach scale is a key step for the integrated assessment of hydromorphologically relevant physical conditions and biological communities.
the GUS is a flexible and adaptable method to characterise physical habitats and flume morphological conditions.

the geomorphic units approach provides a flexible, adaptable and effective method to characterise and assess physical habitats and fl uvial hydromorphism, and therefore to better establish links between physical conditions, geomorphic units, physical habitats and biological conditions at the reach and catchment scales.
